question: What is the main benefit of regional anaesthesia compared to general anaesthesia during childbirth?

options.A: It requires no monitoring of the baby's heartbeat
options.B: Labour progresses twice as fast for every woman
options.C: The mother stays awake during the birth
options.D: It completely prevents any postpartum bleeding

explanation: Regional anaesthesia numbs the lower body while keeping the mother fully conscious to experience the delivery. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why must a midwife check baseline maternal and foetal vitals before giving a regional block?

options.A: To calculate the exact birth weight of the baby beforehand
options.B: To establish a reference point to spot sudden changes later
options.C: To decide which clothes the mother should wear in theatre
options.D: To ensure the mother has not eaten any food recently

explanation: Recording baseline observations allows midwives to quickly identify dangerous drops in blood pressure or foetal distress after the block takes effect. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which type of regional block uses a tiny plastic tube left in place for continuous pain relief?
explanation: An epidural catheter remains in the epidural space so local anaesthetic can be given continuously throughout a long labour. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why is a spinal block preferred over an epidural for an emergency Caesarean section that needs to happen immediately?

options.A: It lets the mother walk around the theatre room
options.B: It completely avoids all risks of low blood pressure
options.C: It does not require any sterile equipment
options.D: It works much faster than an epidural

explanation: Spine medication goes straight into the spinal fluid, producing surgical numbness in minutes compared to the slower onset of an epidural. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h2)

question: How often should maternal blood pressure be checked immediately after a regional block is given?

options.A: Only when the patient complains of pain

explanation: Frequent early checks are necessary because blood pressure can drop very quickly due to the sudden relaxation of blood vessels. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h3)

question: A woman who just received a spinal block looks pale and says she feels dizzy. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Document the findings in the ward register
options.B: Wait ten minutes to see if the dizziness stops
options.C: Ask her to stand up and walk around the room

explanation: Dizziness and paleness are classic signs of spinal-induced low blood pressure, which requires urgent assessment and management. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is a frequent side effect of using opioids in regional anaesthesia blocks?
explanation: Severe itching is a very common side effect when opioids are added to epidural or spinal local anaesthetics. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why do women often need a urinary catheter after receiving an epidural block?

options.A: Kidneys produce three times more urine once the block is placed
options.B: The medication temporarily stops them from feeling when their bladder is full
options.C: It prevents the baby from moving down the birth canal too quickly
options.D: It stops postpartum bleeding from entering the bladder

explanation: Nerve blocks numb the bladder sensation and muscles, making it difficult for the mother to urinate naturally on her own. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h4)

question: What happens during a high or total spinal block complication?

options.A: The baby is born with extra fingers and toes from the medicine
options.B: The mother develops severe high blood pressure and a fast heart rate
options.C: The breathing muscles become weak because the drug reaches the upper chest
options.D: The local anaesthetic completely fails to relieve any labour pain

explanation: When anaesthetic spreads too high, it affects the nerves controlling the diaphragm and chest muscles, slowing normal breathing. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical sign of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST)?

options.B: Passing large amounts of clear urine

explanation: Urine output changes are not a sign of LAST; the condition affects the central nervous and cardiovascular systems directly. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of a post-dural puncture headache after a spinal block?

options.A: Too much caffeine consumed before coming to the hospital
options.B: High blood sugar levels during the first stage of labour
options.C: An allergic reaction to the surgical theatre soap
options.D: Leakage of cerebrospinal fluid from the puncture site

explanation: A small hole in the dura lets fluid leak out, lowering pressure around the brain and causing a severe upright headache. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why must a midwife check leg movement before allowing a post-Caesarean mother to walk to the bathroom?

options.A: To confirm the regional block has worn off enough to prevent falls
options.B: To check if her stitches are healing without any wound infection
options.C: To make sure she has not developed a blood clot in her calf
options.D: To test if her kidneys are producing enough waste products

explanation: Remaining numbness and muscle weakness increase the risk of the mother collapsing if she tries to stand up too early. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h6)
